I didn't have much of an opinion on this topic until I decided to check out the science behind it and one thing in particular swayed me hard. When the sun releases energy or heat it's in the form of shortwave radiation. That heat is then absorbed and reflected or reemitted by planets in the form of longwave or infrared radiation. The reason this is relevant is CO2 and our atmospheric greenhouse gases in general. CO2 has a unique and critical characteristic that can be experimentally proven. CO2 does not react to shortwave radiation, but it absorbs and reemit longwave radiation. In other words it ends up letting the shortwave radiation/heat of the sun go through but then keeps it trapped inside our atmosphere when it's reemitted by the earth in the form of longwave radiation.

If you put CO2 in an atmosphere it's going to result in a warming effect because of this simple phenomena. Now there are a million confounding variables that can change the degree of warmth (or even mask it entirely in extreme circumstances) but all other things being equal, more CO2 means more trapped heat means temperature raising over time. Over the past 400,000 years or so the Earth had stabilized into a fairly regular peak and valley of CO2 levels. The industrial revolution changed all that and the addition of human created CO2 has sent levels higher than they've been in hundreds of thousands of years.

Ultimately I don't think the fact we keep constantly beating heat records is a coincidence. What will this culminate in? I'm not sure but I am sure that continuing to pump large amounts of CO2 into the atmosphere is something that's steadily increasing the probability of substantially undesirable consequences.
